Code notes:

The "_MUSICBEAT variable contains the current beat of the song (with decimals). It uses the blue timer block to be very accurate. Change the 1.9 to affect the speed, and the 8.7 depending on when the first beat starts in your audio track.

The fancy edit effect is characterized by high speed at the beginning and end of each clip, and slowed down completely in the middle (of each clip).
This is similar to the behavior of the "tan" function. And "tan(180x-90)" gives the input range we need, that is at (0, -infinity), (0.5, 0) and (1, infinity). Put each beat as input, and you get an output "tan" you can use to modify direction, size, etc.

Another trick in this project is motion blur. Create two clones with high ghost effect like 80, and have them position slightly in-front-of and slightly behind the main sprite. The result is it looks like motion blur.

The final trick is using the fisheye and whirl effect to make a cool effect. A lot of projects are starting to use these blocks and they are great! Sometimes you need to edit the boundaries of the costume so that it looks right (the center of the costume is the center of the fisheye/whirl effect)
